1. We present an efficient implementation on FPGAs of Finite-Difference (FD) computing engine for acoustic wave modelling, 2. We optimize FD schemes by using optimized FD coefficients and group-alignment technology, 3.
the optimized FD computing engine on FPGAs can be used to solve a variety of problems in science and engineering, including acoustic wave modeling problems.

the optimization of FD computing engines on FPGA-based computing platforms, and we have achieved a high-performance computing engine that has a very low cost of hardware implementation and is very efficient for real-time applications.

a single FPGA can now be able to solve large-scale problems with 2.5 million grid points in 2-D and 1.5 billion grid points in 3-D.
we are able to achieve the best trade-off between numerical accuracy, speed and resource utilization.

the proposed optimized FD schemes are more efficient than conventional FD schemes in terms of the number of on-chip resources and execution time, while maintaining the same accuracy.
